beats.label: S1 · The way in
beats.text: Idealistic Catherine arrives to find Peter cruel and vain; when he burns her school, she learns the throne passes to her if he dies heirless — and starts plotting.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Establishes Catherine, Peter and the coup premise that drives every subsequent season.

beats.label: S1 · Building the circle
beats.text: She recruits maid Marial, bureaucrat Orlo and general Velementov, and falls genuinely in love with Leo, the lover Peter assigns her.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Introduces the inner circle whose loyalties and betrayals dominate S2 and S3.

beats.label: S1 · Reform fails
beats.text: Peter softens after a poisoning and Catherine hopes to reform him — until he burns her pox-inoculating friend Vlad alive with the other infected serfs.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Kills off the 'change him from within' path and locks Catherine into overthrow.

beats.label: S1 · Leo signs on
beats.text: At the Swedish peace talks Catherine rescues Peter's diplomacy; Leo learns of the coup from Marial and returns to Moscow committed to it.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Puts Leo inside the plot, setting up his hostage-taking at the finale.

beats.label: S1 · Peter falls for her
beats.text: The conspirators kill Count Gorky and endure court-wide torture to keep the plot secret; Peter, now besotted, tells Catherine he loves her.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Peter's love — and Catherine's slow reciprocation — is the engine of S2.

beats.label: S1 · The plot cracks
beats.text: On her 21st birthday Catherine finds she is pregnant and moves to strike, but Orlo botches killing Archie and a furious Marial betrays the plot to Peter.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Marial's betrayal and the pregnancy define Catherine's stance heading into the coup and S2.

beats.label: S1 · Fire the shot
beats.text: Peter unveils Leo as his hostage: call off the coup or Leo dies. Catherine says goodbye to Leo, then signals Velementov to fire anyway.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The cliffhanger itself — Leo's fate and the coup start S2.

cliffhanger.text: Catherine has just fired the starting gun on a coup she cannot recall, knowing Leo is Peter's prisoner and Marial has betrayed her — all while carrying Peter's unborn child.
questions: Is Leo still alive after Catherine gave the signal?
Will the army and nobles rally to Catherine or to Peter?
Can Catherine trust anyone in her circle after Marial's turn?

characters.name: Catherine
characters.line: Young empress-in-waiting who has just triggered a coup she can no longer stop, secretly carrying Peter's child.

characters.name: Peter III
characters.line: Volatile emperor who has genuinely fallen in love with Catherine and is holding her lover Leo hostage.

characters.name: Marial
characters.line: Catherine's demoted-noble maid and closest confidante, who just betrayed the plot to Peter to regain her title.

characters.name: Leo Voronsky
characters.line: Catherine's tender lover, gifted to her by Peter and now Peter's prisoner in an unknown state.

characters.name: Orlo
characters.line: Bookish bureaucrat conspirator, wounded and hiding after failing to assassinate Archie.

characters.name: General Velementov
characters.line: General won to the coup, who just fired the signal shot that launched the uprising.

characters.name: Aunt Elizabeth
characters.line: Peter's serene, mystic aunt, fiercely protective of him and the throne he sits on.

characters.name: Archbishop Archie
characters.line: Cynical Patriarch of the Russian church, who survived Orlo's attack and now knows Catherine plotted his death.

characters.name: Grigor
characters.line: Peter's devoted best friend, quietly wounded by Peter's ongoing affair with Grigor's own wife.

characters.name: Georgina
characters.line: Peter's longtime mistress and Grigor's wife, uneasy about losing Peter's favour to Catherine.

beats.label: S2 · Abdication and a bag
beats.text: Four months into the standoff Peter surrenders and signs the abdication — then hands Catherine a bag containing Leo's severed head.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Confirms Leo's death and gives Catherine the throne on Peter's terms, setting the season's uneasy footing.

beats.label: S2 · The reformer takes power
beats.text: Catherine crowns herself, decrees religious freedom and opens her girls' school, installing Leo's gentle cousin Basil over a fuming Archie.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Catherine's reform agenda and her fight with Archie define the season's political spine.

beats.label: S2 · She starts wanting him
beats.text: Coached by Elizabeth to be a mystery, Peter draws Catherine into his bed; unsettled to want him, she keeps him captive while their marriage warms.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The core relationship pivot: Catherine's grief for Leo bleeds into real desire for Peter.

beats.label: S2 · Serf 'jape' backfires
beats.text: A stunt to free the serfs triggers a bloody rebellion; her optimism cracks and Marial executes Lady Svenska in revenge for a murdered servant.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Catherine's first real failure as empress; Marial's killing shows how far the coup has hardened her.

beats.label: S2 · Joanna arrives, and dies
beats.text: Catherine's imperious mother Joanna arrives to belittle her and seduce Peter for her own dynastic plot; mid-tryst Joanna falls from a window and dies.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Joanna's death is the secret Peter carries; it becomes the fault line of the finale.

beats.label: S2 · The secret spills
beats.text: Peter and Elizabeth hide Joanna's death; Russia goes to war with the Ottomans, and a jilted Marial finally tells Catherine what Peter did.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Puts the war and Catherine's rage into place for the finale's arrests and stabbing.

beats.label: S2 · She stabs the wrong man
beats.text: At Marial's wedding Catherine has the conspirators arrested and stabs Peter in his chambers — only to find she has killed his body double, Pugachev.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The body-double reveal is the cliffhanger itself and the seed of S3's rebellion.

cliffhanger.text: Catherine sits on the throne surrounded by friends she has just arrested, married to a man she has just tried to murder — who is very much alive because he swapped in a body double, Pugachev, whose body now cools on the floor.
questions: Can Catherine and Peter share a throne after she tried to kill him?
What becomes of Marial, Grigor and the other arrested nobles?
Will Peter forgive her or retaliate for the attempt on his life?

characters.name: Catherine
characters.line: Empress who has just tried to murder Peter but stabbed his double instead; she and Peter now uneasily embrace.

characters.name: Peter III
characters.line: Deposed emperor, deeply in love with Catherine, hiding that he accidentally killed her mother.

characters.name: Marial
characters.line: Restored noblewoman just arrested for revealing Peter's crime; she and Catherine are estranged again.

characters.name: Aunt Elizabeth
characters.line: Peter's aunt and Catherine's advisor, actively covering up Joanna's death alongside Peter.

characters.name: Archbishop Archie
characters.line: Patriarch in an uneasy peace with Catherine after failing to keep his hold on the court.

characters.name: Grigor
characters.line: Peter's best friend, arrested at the wedding, torn between loyalty to Peter and his affair with Marial.

characters.name: Georgina
characters.line: Peter's exiled ex-mistress, back at court and conspicuously not arrested tonight.

characters.name: Orlo
characters.line: Fallen bureaucrat, left court in disgrace after being caught stealing from the treasury for his home region.

characters.name: General Velementov
characters.line: General now running Catherine's newly declared Ottoman war.

characters.name: Paul
characters.line: Catherine and Peter's newborn son and Russia's heir.

beats.label: S3 · Loyalty at gunpoint
beats.text: Catherine, guilt-ridden over Pugachev, tests the freed conspirators by ordering Georgina to shoot first; Georgina kills Tatyana to prove her loyalty.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Shows Catherine trying to be ruthless and resets the court's pecking order around her.

beats.label: S3 · Orlo in the woods
beats.text: Enraged that Peter still lives, Orlo disavows Catherine and storms off; hunting in the woods, she unknowingly shoots him dead.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Removes Catherine's oldest conspirator by her own hand — a private wound she'll carry through the season.

beats.label: S3 · Playing the game
beats.text: Coached by Elizabeth and Archie to play the game, Catherine convenes the Nakaz to hear her people, but reform keeps colliding with their fear.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Shows her new pragmatic method — and its limits — and pushes her back toward alliances she distrusts.

beats.label: S3 · Archie builds a fake Peter
beats.text: Archie secretly grooms the peasant Pugachev to impersonate Peter and raise a rebellion, planning to 'save' Catherine and regain his hold on her.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The engine of the entire back half: every crisis Catherine faces from here is Archie's design.

beats.label: S3 · Peter through the ice
beats.text: Goaded by King Hugo, Peter steals Catherine's army to invade Sweden; on a frozen lake they declare their love, then he plunges through the ice and drowns.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Peter's death removes the show's other lead; every following beat is Catherine coping with the hole.

beats.label: S3 · The fantasy breaks
beats.text: Catherine hides Peter's death behind a fantasy that he is off at war, until Elizabeth's vision and Grigor's collapse force her to accept he is gone.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The grief turn that hardens her into the empress she becomes by the finale.

beats.label: S3 · Buried and beheaded
beats.text: Marial exposes Archie as Pugachev's puppeteer; Catherine crushes the rebellion, has Archie beheaded and emerges truly in command — while Marial secretly revives him.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Resolves the rebellion and Catherine's arc, and leaves the covert Archie thread live.

cliffhanger.text: Peter is dead, the rebellion is crushed and Catherine finally rules with the confidence of an empress — but Archie has been secretly revived by Marial, Paul is still an infant, and the court around her is thinned and wary.
questions: What happens when Archie's secret survival surfaces?
Can Catherine raise Paul as her heir without Peter?
Where do Marial, Grigor and Georgina belong now that Peter is gone?

characters.name: Catherine
characters.line: Empress transformed by grief and rebellion; ruling alone, in command, and no longer trusting easily.

characters.name: Peter III
characters.line: Recently dead after falling through ice; his absence now defines the throne and Catherine's next chapter.

characters.name: Aunt Elizabeth
characters.line: Peter's aunt and Catherine's mystic advisor, who watched her grow into power and stood down from taking it herself.

characters.name: Marial
characters.line: Catherine's friend again, hiding a huge secret: she has just revived the Archbishop Catherine ordered killed.

characters.name: Archbishop Archie
characters.line: Officially executed for backing Pugachev's rebellion, secretly alive in Marial's care.

characters.name: Grigor
characters.line: Chose Marial over Georgina, still hollowed out by grief for Peter.

characters.name: Georgina
characters.line: Tried to marry the infant Paul to seize power; caught by Grigor, sidelined but not punished.

characters.name: Paul
characters.line: Infant heir, briefly kidnapped and passed around during the rebellion before being returned to Catherine.

characters.name: Maxim
characters.line: Marial's unstable child-husband, who believes he killed Pugachev and has joined Catherine's inner circle.
